errors.text: The proposed 10 h milling and 1100 °C SPS conditions substantially miss the target window of 1–6 h milling and 900–1000 °C sintering; these harsher conditions increase contamination, decomposition, and grain-coarsening risks.

No quantitative displacement or strain-rate regime is defined, despite the request to incorporate displacement-rate and thermal-expansion constraints and identify where dual-phase stability is maximized.
The falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary strengthening from solute strengthening. It primarily tests whether rapid sintering affects HCP formation and hardness.
The falsification logic is inverted: poorer properties after a longer dwell or slower heating would support, rather than falsify, the claim that rapid SPS is beneficial.
The cited evidence concerns materially different HEA systems and does not substantiate the specific 1100 °C, greater-than-100 °C/min CoCrFeNiTi processing window.
